label: Mid/late original-phase input of s/t/v/q/k/w/p/u/1/y (first occurrence) after h/o/r/0/3/j/f/b appeared earlier; also <DEL>
explanation: Fires mostly during the original phase (86% of mass), peaking at t=3-6, plus on the <DEL> step (12% of mass, about 10% rate). It is almost silent in the copy phase (2% of mass) and never fires at t=0. The current input token matters most: s (25% rate, 5x lift, and the top activations are nearly all s), then t and v (about 17%), then q, k, w, p, u, 1, y. It prefers first occurrences of the token (in_first carries 90% of mass). Activation is higher when the earlier prefix contains tokens from the set h, o, r, 0, 3, j, f, b (first_tok in this set gives about 2.2x lift). Requiring two or more of them raises precision to about 0.55 but cuts recall. The rule is a soft conjunction of input-token identity and prefix composition, and no clean boolean rule captures it: dev F1 is 0.47 and mass recall 0.65. Adding <DEL> steps adds recall but lowers precision.
